rv.q: But for such a starry cast Tamara Harvey's production has a disappointing lack of sparkle.
Instead, both the orchard and this production will be lost to time. And you leave feeling the woman at the centre could have done more to save them.
Harvey's assured direction combined with the evocative design and a superb ensemble cast elevate material that can sadly at times feel static.
It is an entirely one-note performance, and a discordant one at that. Luckily, it is the only false note in the cast.

At least, I thought it would be, until two high-profile productions were announced to be gracing the stages of the UK this year. First up is the RSC, staging a new adaptation written by Laura Wade, whose previous RSC work (also directed by Tamara Harvey), The Constant Wife , was a tremendous hit.
There's an almost total lack of emotion, rendering this remarkable play cold and – dare I say it – largely dull.
